headline: Australian government gas reservation policies could redirect domestic producers toward higher-value LNG export markets, creating opportunity for east coast gas suppliers
reasoning: If proposed government gas reservation policies are enacted in their current form, LNG producers would be required to supply more gas into the domestic market, which McCaul argues would logically push smaller producers like Comet Ridge toward the LNG export market instead. This dynamic could also incentivise LNG schemes to invest in new upstream gas supply to meet their mandated 20% domestic requirement. The Australian Energy Market Operator and others have flagged a looming supply shortfall from the early 2030s, suggesting the east coast gas market will be tight and well-positioned new supply projects will have strong pricing power across both domestic and LNG channels.
quote: I think when we see the government intervening in markets like this and where we have the LNG producers are forced to produce more gas into the domestic market. I think the logical pivot for someone like Comet Ridge is to then push more of our gas into the LNG market, and we're in a pretty good position given where about 240 KS inland of Gladstone. So we have a major trunk line running into LNG, about 80 KS to the south of us. We also have Germany's domestic line about the same distance to the south. So we'll have access to domestic pipeline and LNG export pipeline near our project. And that means we can go either way.

headline: MD outlines Mahalo Gas project strategy after acquiring 100% ownership, targeting FID in Q1 2026 and first gas in late 2028
reasoning: Comet Ridge has acquired 100% of the Mahalo Gas project in central Queensland (1,850 km²) after buying out Origin LNG and Santos over recent years. The fully-owned structure allows the company to develop the field holistically based on geology rather than joint venture block boundaries. Phase one development targets 50 TJ/day of gas supply, with one contract already signed with CleanCo (up to 10 TJ/day), leaving 40 TJ/day still to be contracted. Key milestones include passing through the NAIF funding gate, securing gas sales agreements, and reaching a final investment decision in Q1 next year, with first gas expected in late 2028. Proximity to both domestic pipeline infrastructure and the Gladstone LNG export terminal gives optionality to sell into either domestic or international markets. Government gas reservation policies could further benefit Comet Ridge by allowing it to redirect more gas toward higher-priced LNG export markets.

So we're about to enter a DD phase and pass through the second gate, which is basically the funding gate. We're also seeing interest from commercial banks coming back into the gas market.
